text.label: Heading: This book was written for two people. You are probably one o
text.value: This book was written for two people. You are probably one of them.

text.label: Text: The spot you are in.
text.value: The spot you are in.

text.label: Text: You are a coach, an author, a speaker or an influencer. You
text.value: You are a coach, an author, a speaker or an influencer. You know something other people want to learn, and you have spent years getting good at it. People watch you. Some of them quote you back to yourself. And when you look at your bank account, it does not look like your follower count. If that is you, nothing is wrong with you and nothing is wrong with what you teach. You are standing in a spot a lot of talented people are standing in, and nobody ever showed you the way out of it.

text.label: Text: An audience, nothing to sell.
text.value: An audience, nothing to sell.

text.label: Text: The first version of that spot is a crowd with nothing to bu
text.value: The first version of that spot is a crowd with nothing to buy. You have 5,000, 10,000, maybe 50,000 followers. They like what you say. They would pay you for more of it if there were something to pay for. There is not. No program, no course, no book with your name on the cover. So the attention arrives every day and leaves every day, and all you have to show for it is a number on a screen that belongs to somebody else.

text.label: Text: Something to sell, no hours.
text.value: Something to sell, no hours.

text.label: Text: The second version is harder to see, because money is coming
text.value: The second version is harder to see, because money is coming in. You have a program or a course, and it sells. But it only sells when you answer every message yourself. A person asks what it costs on a Saturday night, and you see it three days later. You make sales when you launch something, and it goes quiet in between. You could not hand me ten names and phone numbers of the people watching you. The business works exactly as hard as you do, and it stops when you stop.

text.label: Text: The two readers.
text.value: The two readers.

text.label: Text: Chapter one talks to two readers in turn. One has built an a
text.value: Chapter one talks to two readers in turn. One has built an audience and is missing everything that goes behind it. The other has no audience yet. I tell that second reader something they do not expect: you are not behind. You get to build the system first and open the doors after, the way a franchise is built. The first stranger who ever finds you will have a place to land, a way to leave a name and something to buy. Most people with big followings cannot say that.

text.label: Text: Not a talent problem.
text.value: Not a talent problem.

text.label: Text: I want to be plain about this, because you may have been bla
text.value: I want to be plain about this, because you may have been blaming yourself. Getting attention is one skill. Turning it into income is a different skill. Being very good at the first tells you nothing about the second. The people I talk to are clearly good at what they do. What is missing is the part that goes behind the audience, and that part can be written down, in order, in plain words. That is what this book is.

text.value: Getting attention is one skill. Turning it into income is a different skill.

text.value: The whole plan.

text.label: Text: Think about what a blueprint does for a house. It shows ever
text.value: Think about what a blueprint does for a house. It shows every room, where the doors go, what holds the roof up, and the order the work gets done in. Nobody lays a floor before the foundation. A blueprint is not a tip about windows. It is the whole plan, on paper, before anybody picks up a hammer. This book does that for your business. It is the plan for how a person who knows something gets paid for it, start to finish, in the order it gets built.

text.label: Text: Not one tactic.
text.value: Not one tactic.

text.label: Text: You have probably bought tactics before. How to grow on one
text.value: You have probably bought tactics before. How to grow on one platform. How to write a caption. How to run an ad. Every one of those is a room, and some of them are good rooms. The trouble is that a room with no house around it does nothing for you. More views with nowhere to send the viewer is a good day and an empty bank account. The book never hands you a room without showing you where it sits in the house.

text.label: Text: One line.
text.value: One line.

text.label: Text: The whole model fits in one line, and it sits under the titl
text.value: The whole model fits in one line, and it sits under the title on the cover. Attention + Your Product = Dollars. Attention is the people watching and listening to you. Your product is what you know, packaged so a person can buy it. Dollars are what you get when you send the first to the second, on a website you own. Attention by itself does not pay you. A product by itself does not pay you either. A good course nobody hears about is a store on a road with no cars.

text.label: Text: Every part of it.
text.value: Every part of it.

text.label: Text: So the blueprint covers all of it. How you get the attention
text.value: So the blueprint covers all of it. How you get the attention, on platforms that send you no bill. How you take what is in your head and turn it into something with a name and a price. Where the sale happens, which is a website with your name in the address. And the six business systems behind that website that answer every person, follow up, ask for the review and ask for the sale. Connected, those six are one Revenue Engine. That is a business model, front to back.

text.label: Text: From plan to house.
text.value: From plan to house.

text.label: Text: A plan is worth what gets built from it, so this one is writ

What the blueprint gives you is the plan itself: what goes where, what comes first, and how to check that each piece works before you build the next one on top of it.

text.value: I did not invent any of this, and the book says so in its first pages. Every business I have owned ran on the same three moves. Be known. Have something worth buying. Keep showing up until the person is ready. The book goes back to a hamburger stand in the 1950s, where two brothers built a way of working that anybody could be taught to run, and to the author who later gave the idea a name: the franchise prototype. The system runs the business. People run the system.

text.label: Text: What it used to take.
text.value: What it used to take.

text.label: Text: Here is why that idea was never yours to use. A system like
text.value: Here is why that idea was never yours to use. A system like the one at that hamburger stand needed three things. It needed a building for customers to walk into. It needed a payroll, because a person had to take every order and answer every question. And it needed an advertising budget, because the only way to reach a stranger was to pay for the space. I learned that in 1986, the year I opened a restaurant. When the money stopped, the strangers stopped with it. A person whose whole business is something they know had none of the three.

text.label: Text: Free airtime.
text.value: Free airtime.

text.label: Text: Today you can go live on five different social media platfor
text.value: Today you can go live on five different social media platforms and nobody sends you a bill. That is airtime, every day, for anybody holding a phone, and the book treats it that way. It has you pick one question your buyers ask, answer it on camera, and end by saying your own website address out loud. You can put out your own show. You can publish your own book and sell it from your own website, which is what I did with this one. I have watched forty years of tools arrive, and never in that time has so much been available to one person at such a low price.

text.label: Text: The work gets done.
text.value: The work gets done.

text.label: Text: The second change is the bigger one. Every tool I ever put t
text.value: The second change is the bigger one. Every tool I ever put to work made a person faster. The fax did not write the letter. The website did not answer the question. A human still had to do the job, which is why growing always meant hiring. An AI employee is the first tool in forty years that does the work. It reads the message, writes back, and books a time on your calendar, at 11:40 on a Saturday night. That is what took the payroll out of the plan.

text.label: Text: So why not you.
text.value: So why not you.

text.label: Text: If you are truly an expert at what you do, there should be n
text.value: If you are truly an expert at what you do, there should be no reason you are not making money from it today. I mean that kindly. The stages cost nothing and the staff is no longer a payroll. That leaves two jobs, and the book is laid out around them. Getting your attention and your product to meet is the work of Part Two and Part Three. Telling the world is chapter seven. Plenty of very good people are waiting to be discovered. Nobody is coming to discover you. That job is yours now.

text.label: Text: The plain word.
text.value: The plain word.

text.label: Text: There is a plain word for telling the world, and I use it in
text.value: There is a plain word for telling the world, and I use it in the book. Self-promotion. People cannot buy from somebody they have never heard of. For most of my working life that meant buying an ad. Today it means showing up and teaching what you know, where people are already watching, with every clip pointing home to the website you own. It does not matter what you do for a living. You have to do it. The book shows you how to do it on a schedule, so it does not eat your week.

text.label: Text: Your part.
text.value: Your part.

text.label: Text: Here is the honest split. Getting good at what you teach too
text.value: Here is the honest split. Getting good at what you teach took you years. Call it your ten thousand hours. No book can hand them to you, and that is what makes them worth so much. A talent agent stands behind real talent. He does not manufacture it. You have already put those hours in, or you are putting them in now. The blueprint is everything else. Where the attention goes, what you sell, how it gets sold, and who does the work while you sleep. You bring the reps. The book brings the rest.

text.value: If you are truly an expert at what you do, there should be no reason you are not making money from it today.
